summary: CCD sits where three markets meet: India's underground dance music scene (nights, artists, promoters), scene media and discovery (Wild City, Resident Advisor's India guides, Homegrown, ticketing apps), and culture-led streetwear drops. Ticketing apps (District, Insider, HighApe, SortMyScene, Skillbox) own transactions and run heavy Meta ads for promoters' nights; scene media owns editorial; nobody combines curated nights, a national scene platform, artist booking and limited drops under one brand with a music-first identity. CCD's live platform already does more than most competitors, but it has gaps that leak demand: points with no redemption, curated events that link offsite, no check-in or pre-event reminders.

opportunities.opportunity: Make the owned list the engine: every Episode RSVP, drop and Discover visit feeds email + WhatsApp, and the weekly digest becomes the reason to stay
opportunities.evidence: Episodes are free RSVP (so the RSVP is the conversion), and the platform already has early access, WhatsApp opt-in and a weekly digest

opportunities.opportunity: Fix the leaks before buying traffic: points redemption, pre-event WhatsApp reminders, check-in, and on-site pages for curated events
opportunities.evidence: The README lists these as gaps and calls the missing redemption a broken promise

opportunities.opportunity: Sell limited drops off the back of Episodes and the founder's 150k page, with scarcity that's real (no restocks)
opportunities.evidence: Drops are limited and screen-printed; scarcity is a true proof point

opportunities.opportunity: Win the artist side first: artists claiming profiles and sharing their Episode content bring their fans
opportunities.evidence: For Artists offer (recordings, content, 200-400 listening room) is stronger than anything competitors pitch to artists

opportunities.opportunity: Per-city scene guides and per-event pages as the citable source for underground events in India
